PRAYER in W.A.SR.No.91974 of 2024

The Writ Appeal is filed under Clause 15 of the Letters Patent to   the order dated 08.09.2021 passed in W.P.No.2993 of 2015 by this court.
 For Appellant(s): Mr.R.Murali  For Respondent(s) Mr.Ramanlal, Addl.Adv.General  Assisted by  Mr.Vadivel Deenadayalan,
 Addl.Govt.Pleader  ORDER (Order of the Court was made by J.NISHA BANU, J.) The Civil Miscellaneous Petition has been filed to condone the delay of 979 days in filing the Writ Appeal.

2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Additional Advocate General,
assisted by the Additional Government Pleader appearing for the respondent.
3.
The above appeal has been filed against the order dated 08.09.2021 made in W.P.No.2993 of 2015 passed by this Court.
The petitioner herein filed https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

( Uploaded on: 05/08/2025 05:45:16 pm ) WA SR No.91974 of 2024 and the above writ petition seeking direction to the respondents to pay compensation, passing appropriate award for its lands situated in various survey numbers measuring to an extent of 3.91 acres, as per Section 24(2) of the Right to fair compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and resettlement Act, 2013,
within the time limit as fixed by this court.

entities.text: Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The said writ petition was dismissed.

However, it was observed by the learned Single Judge as " if the petitioner proves title over the subject properties,
which were gifted in favour of the third respondent which was subsequently cancelled through cancellation deed, before civil court, he can claim compensation before the authorities concerned ".
Challenging the dismissal order, the present appeal has been filed with a delay of 979 days.
4. Undoubtedly, there is an inordinate delay of 979 days in filing the Appeal.

In the affidavit, it is stated by the petitioner that, the case bundle was mixed up with the other bundles in the office of the earlier counsel and thereafter with an extensive search, it has been found and the same was handed over to the petitioner, however, the original certified copy of the order was found missing.

2 further stated that after getting the certified copy of the order by the earlier counsel, the present appeal has been filed and in such circumstances there occurred a delay of 979 days in filing the appeal. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

sentences.text: ( Uploaded on: 05/08/2025 05:45:16 pm ) WA SR No.91974 of 2024 and 5.
We have carefully examined the above said averments made in the affidavit.
But, we are not satisfied with the above explanation for such inordinate delay in filing the appeal.
Therefore, in the absence of any valid explanation or sufficient cause to condone such enormous delay in filing the appeal, we are not inclined to entertain the petition.

6. It is brought to the notice of this court by the learned counsel for the petitioner that already a civil suit was filed by the land owners, including the petitioner against the Block Development officer/Commissioner, Kundrathu @ Padappa, Kanchipuram District seeking to forbear the respondent and his men from trespassing the property and the same is pending.
7.
Pendency of civil suit has not given any assistance to the petitioner to decide the present petition in its favour.
8. Accordingly, the condone delay petition is dismissed and consequently, the writ appeal is rejected at the SR stage itself.
No costs.
